issues.legal_issue: A co-owner who jointly sought eviction may continue the claim after another co-owner transfers her interest and the transferee opposes eviction, unless a later event ends the co-owners’ collective entitlement.
material_facts: The two co-owners jointly filed suits to evict their tenants.
After the suits were dismissed, one co-owner transferred her share to persons associated with a tenant.
The transferee opposed eviction, while the other co-owner continued to pursue the appeals.
issues.conclusion: The objection did not make the continuing co-owner’s eviction claim incompetent; consent to the joint claim could not be withdrawn midway to prejudice that co-owner.
issues.legal_principle: A co-owner may sue to evict a tenant on behalf of the co-owners under the doctrine of agency, and the other co-owners’ consent is presumed unless disagreement is shown. Once a joint suit is filed, the parties’ rights are ordinarily assessed as of its institution; a later event matters only if it ends the co-owners’ entitlement by act of parties or operation of law. The Court relied on Sri Ram Pasricha v. Jagannath and Dhannalal v. Kalawatibai.

rule.if: coowner_eviction_case and coowners_jointly_sought_eviction and continuing_coowner_pursued_claim and another_coowner_or_successor_opposed_eviction and not collective_entitlement_later_ended

predicates.coowner_eviction_case: The proceeding is a claim by co-owners to evict a tenant from jointly owned property.
predicates.coowners_jointly_sought_eviction: The co-owners jointly sought eviction when the claim was filed.
predicates.continuing_coowner_pursued_claim: One co-owner continued to pursue the eviction claim after it was filed.
predicates.another_coowner_or_successor_opposed_evi: Another co-owner or a successor to that co-owner opposed eviction after the joint claim began.
predicates.collective_entitlement_later_ended: A later event ended the co-owners’ collective entitlement to seek eviction.

issues.definition: When co-owners jointly seek eviction and one continues the claim despite another co-owner’s or successor’s opposition, the continuing co-owner may pursue it unless a later event ended their collective entitlement.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s acquisition of only part of a landlord’s interest does not extinguish the tenancy by merger.
material_facts: The property was jointly owned by two co-owners and let to tenants.
Some partners of one tenant firm acquired the share of one co-owner during the litigation.
The tenant-associated purchasers acquired only a share of the property, not the entire landlord interest.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy was not extinguished by merger because the landlord’s interest did not vest entirely in the tenant’s interest.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 111(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, merger requires the landlord’s interest in its entirety to vest in the tenant’s interest in its entirety. Acquisition of only part of the landlord’s interest, or of one co-landlord’s interest, does not cause merger or extinguish the tenancy.

predicates.landlord_tenant_case: The proceeding concerns a tenancy between a landlord and a tenant.
predicates.tenancy_relationship_exists: A tenancy existed between the parties before the tenant’s acquisition.
predicates.tenant_acquired_only_part_of_landlord_in: The tenant or persons associated with the tenant acquired only part of the landlord’s interest.

issues.definition: If a tenancy exists and the tenant acquires only part of the landlord’s interest, the tenancy is not extinguished by merger.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee who acquires an interest during eviction litigation cannot take an inconsistent position that prejudices the transferring co-owner’s continuing claim.
material_facts: During the appeals, persons associated with a tenant acquired one co-owner’s share in the property.
Those purchasers joined the tenant in opposing eviction, although their predecessor had jointly sought eviction with the remaining co-owner.
The purchasers’ position would have prejudiced the remaining co-owner’s claim against another tenant.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers’ opposition to eviction was immaterial and could not defeat the continuing co-owner’s claim against the other tenant.
issues.legal_principle: The rights of the parties to a jointly filed eviction suit are ordinarily assessed from the date the suit was instituted. A transferee during the litigation cannot use the acquired interest to take a position contrary to the transferor’s position and prejudice the other co-owner’s rights.

predicates.pending_coowner_eviction_case: An eviction proceeding brought by co-owners remained pending when the interest was transferred.
predicates.transferee_acquired_interest_during_liti: A transferee acquired an interest in the property while the eviction proceeding was pending.
predicates.transferor_supported_eviction: The transferring co-owner had supported the eviction claim before transferring the interest.
predicates.transferee_opposed_eviction_to_prejudice: The transferee opposed eviction in a way that would prejudice the remaining co-owner’s claim.

issues.definition: A transferee who acquires an interest during a pending co-owner eviction case cannot defeat the remaining co-owner’s claim by taking an inconsistent position that prejudices that co-owner.

issues.legal_issue: When the underlying land has been divided but the building has not, an eviction decree may be executed against the portion of the building corresponding to the claimant’s share of the land.
material_facts: The co-owners had partitioned the land beneath the building but had not partitioned the building itself.
The co-owners had intended to demolish the existing building and build separately on their respective land shares.
The Court treated the building as corresponding to the divided land and identified the relevant portion for execution of the eviction decree.
issues.conclusion: The eviction decree against the other tenant was executable against the part of the building corresponding to the land allotted to the claimant co-owner.
issues.legal_principle: Invoking Article 142 of the Constitution to avoid further litigation, the Court applied the premise that an unpartitioned superstructure could be treated as going with the land beneath it, so each co-owner was entitled to the corresponding portion of the structure.

rule.if: eviction_decree_execution_case and underlying_land_partitioned and building_unpartitioned and building_portions_correspond_to_land_shares

predicates.eviction_decree_execution_case: The proceeding concerns execution of an eviction decree.
predicates.underlying_land_partitioned: The land beneath the building has been divided among the co-owners.
predicates.building_unpartitioned: The building standing on the land has not itself been divided.
predicates.building_portions_correspond_to_land_sha: The building can be treated as having portions corresponding to the respective land shares.

issues.definition: When an eviction decree is being executed, the underlying land is divided, and the unpartitioned building corresponds to those land shares, the decree may be executed against the corresponding building portion.
